title: Catequesis de la Iglesia Filipina Independiente por el Emmo. Sr. Gregorio Aglipay y Labáyan, Obispo Máximo de dicha Iglesia, aprobada por el Consejo Supremo de Obispos. Prólogo del Pbro. José Ferrándiz
creator: Gregorio Aglipay y Labáyan; prólogo del Pbro. José Ferrándiz
content: A catechism in Spanish of the Iglesia Filipina Independiente, under the name of Gregorio Aglipay y Labáyan as Obispo Máximo and marked as approved by the Supreme Council of Bishops. The title page (lines 13-37) is garbled; a contents list ('Índice') is at lines 198-320. Editorial matter: a prologue signed José Ferrándiz, Presbítero, ends at line 1342, dated Madrid, 25 May 1912. Divisions: the catechism begins at line 1346 with prayers, then doctrine, sacraments and church rules. Regulations for the parish committees begin at line 5777, signed by Aglipay at Manila, 6 August 1903 (line 5835) and 7 August 1903 (line 6101). Errata close the file at lines 6550-6588.
locus: regulations for the committees of gentlemen and the commissions of ladies, signed by Aglipay, at lines 5777-6106; the rest not mapped
flags: Title page garbled in the OCR (lines 13-37): the word 'Catequesis' is not legible there and no imprint or year is printed, so title and publisher are kept from the draft (catalogue record); the only printed date seen is the prologue's, 25 May 1912 (line 1342).

title: Death Struggles of Slavery: a narrative of facts and incidents, which occurred in a British colony, during the two years immediately preceding Negro emancipation. By Henry Bleby, a resident in the colony seventeen years. Third edition
creator: Henry Bleby, a resident in the colony seventeen years
content: The third edition of Henry Bleby's narrative of the two years before emancipation in a British colony; the text is set in Jamaica. Editorial matter: the author's preface to the third edition at lines 46-278, which mentions November 1868. A contents list at lines 279-338 names twenty-eight chapters. Divisions: Chapter I, 'Symptoms of Revolt', begins at line 353 and the text ends at line 14890. Samuel Sharpe is told of in Chapter X, 'Origin of the Revolt' (lines 5168-5970): Edward Hylton's account of the meeting and the oath, Sharpe's own statements to the author, his execution at Montego Bay on 23 May 1832, and the author's judgment of him.
locus: Edward Hylton's account of Sam Sharpe's meeting and the oath at lines 5515-5609; Sharpe's execution and the author's last conversation with him at lines 5826-5894; the rest not mapped
flags: The title page prints only 'London. 1868.' with no publisher's name; the printer's line at the end (line 14893, 'London: printed by') is cut off, so the draft's 'W. Nichols' could not be confirmed from the file.

title: The Taeping Rebellion in China; a narrative of its rise and progress. Based upon original documents and information obtained in China
creator: Commander Lindesay Brine, R.N., F.R.G.S., lately employed in Chinese waters
content: A narrative of the Taeping rebellion, with map and plans. Editorial matter: the author's preface at lines 97-394. Contents at lines 395-522, a list of illustrations at line 523. title: The Druzes and the Maronites under the Turkish Rule from 1840 to 1860

content: An account of the Druzes and the Maronites of the Lebanon from 1840 to the massacres of 1860, by an author who says he lived in the Lebanon through most of that period. Editorial matter: a note on the impression at lines 61-68 and the author's preface at lines 76-153, signed Charles Henry Churchill, Beyrout, Syria. Contents at lines 156-234. Divisions: nine chapters, Chapter I from line 236; the text ends at line 8731. The Maronite patriarch is spoken of many times, for example at lines 1343-1507 and 3871-3883, and in the heading of Chapter IV, but always by office: the file does not name Peter Paul Massaad. An advertisement for the author's 'Mount Lebanon' follows from line 8739.
locus: Chapter IV, whose heading names the 'Intolerance of the Maronite Patriarch', at lines 3055-4139; the rest not mapped
flags: A bookseller's advertisement (Quaritch) follows the text from line 8739; library pocket slip at the very end.

title: Seven Lectures on the Second Coming of the Lord. Delivered in Toronto, in 1863, by J. N. Darby. From revised notes

content: Seven lectures on the second coming of the Lord, printed from revised notes of lectures given in Toronto in 1863. title: Biographical Dictionary of Ministers and Preachers of the Welsh Calvinistic Methodist Body or Presbyterians of Wales
creator: Rev. Joseph Evans, Denbigh
publisher: Carnarvon: D. O'Brien Owen, C. M. Book Agency
content: A dictionary in English of short lives of ministers and preachers of the Welsh Calvinistic Methodists, arranged alphabetically by surname and printed in two columns. Editorial matter: the compiler's preface at lines 97-181, dated Denbigh, October 1907, and a bibliography of his sources, mostly Welsh, at lines 185-393. Divisions: the entries run from line 404 (Abraham, Mr. Rowlant); an appendix of further entries begins at line 35018 and errata at line 35166. The entry 'Jones, Rev Thomas, Khassia, Assam' is at lines 19884-19971: it gives his birth in 1810, his ordination at Bala in 1840, his arrival at Cherrapoonjee in 1841, the end of his connection with the Society in 1847 and his death at Calcutta in 1849, with references.
locus: entry for Jones, Rev Thomas, Khassia, at lines 19884-19971; the rest not mapped
flags: The title page prints no year (the only date is the preface's, October 1907, line 181); small words of the title ('of', 'or') are lost in the OCR at lines 21-28 and were supplied from the page's sense and the running heads; a New York Public Library stamp follows the title page.

title: A Narrative of the Persecution of the Christians in Madagascar; with details of the escape of the six Christian refugees now in England. By J. J. Freeman and D. Johns, formerly missionaries in the island. Sixth thousand
creator: J. J. Freeman and D. Johns, formerly missionaries in the island
content: A narrative by two former missionaries of the persecution of Christians in Madagascar. Editorial matter: an explanation of the frontispiece at lines 60-93 and a preface from line 96. Chapter VII (lines 6051-7613) runs from the queen's edict of 1 March 1835 to the martyrdom of Rasalama, with Rasalama from line 7045 and her name explained at line 7585. flags: The contents list dates Rasalama's martyrdom '1837?' with a query in the head of Chapter VIII (line 322); publisher's advertisements from line 12129 and a Library of Congress preservation slip dated 2005 at the end.

content: A French translation from Amharic of a chronicle of the reign of Ménélik II, with illustrations, maps and plans. The title page is printed twice (lines 72-113 and 142-193). Atié Johannès comes to Choa and makes peace with Atié Ménélik in Chapter XXVI. Taïtou is named from the introduction (line 261) onward, for example at lines 32577-32580 and in the notes at lines 35377-35543.
locus: Chapter XXVI, Atié Johannès arrives in Choa and makes peace with Atié Ménélik, at lines 23580-25585; Chapter XXVII, the assembly held at Borou-Miéda, at lines 25586-26867; the rest not mapped
flags: A microfilm reproduction: University of California, Berkeley, Library Photographic Service notices at lines 13-67 and 62980-62994, with a test chart marked 1963.
